launches.tagline: Build and deploy complex AI agents with any model and any tool in just 5 lines of code. No Docker files. No YAMLs. No wasted weeks.
launches.body:
# [**TL;DR:**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E0FR4LBTSZo)

_We’re excited to launch [Dedalus Labs](https://www.dedaluslabs.ai/), an AI-native cloud platform for developers to build agentic AI applications. Our [SDKs](https://github.com/dedalus-labs/dedalus-sdk-python) allows you to connect any LLM to any MCP servers – local or remotely hosted by us. No Docker files or YAML configs required._

* **Blog:** https://dedaluslabs.ai/blog/dedalus-seed-round
* **Product Demos:**
  * https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s2khf1Monho
  * https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4B1xuRCgLgA

# **The Problem: Building Agents Is Hard**

Building tool-using agents ≠ calling **_v1/chat/completions._**

Today, developers are still stuck with:

* Running their MCP servers locally.
* If deploying remotely, wiring up AWS and config hell.
* Juggling model quirks, streaming issues, and auth across GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Sonnet, Flash, etc. (♾️ API keys).
* Rebuilding everything just to add a new tool.

We were **_tired_** of writing hundreds of lines of code and battling Docker files and infra—all for a spaghetti agent that breaks under stress.

**So, we built the tool we wished existed.**

# **What We Offer: Complex Agents in 5 Lines of Code**

Dedalus invented the simplest way to build and deploy agents—a drop-in infrastructure layer that unifies models, tools, and orchestration.

Our open-source SDK supports:

* Vendor-agnostic model handoffs
* Chaining both local tools and hosted MCPs
* Real-time streaming across any provider

—all in 5 lines of code.

And our managed infra lets you **deploy an MCP server in 3 clicks**, so anyone can equip their agent with tools. No Docker files, no setup.

# **Why MCP: Tools Made for Agents**

[MCP (Model Context Protocol)](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io/) is becoming the standard for how models talk to tools. Think of it as an API that AI models already know how to call—reliable, predictable, and language-agnostic.

As more companies adopt MCP, exposing your product as an MCP server means you’re not just serving humans anymore—you’re serving _agents._

We’re building the infrastructure that powers that shift.

# **Our Story: Two Princeton CS Students with High Standards**

We’re **Cathy** (ex-Voyage AI / Salesforce) and **Windsor** (ex-DeepMind / Sentient AGI).

We first ran into this problem while working with MCP during Windsor’s time at Sentient AGI. Every solution felt wrong: drag-and-drop GUIs, brittle configs, frameworks that broke under real workloads. Nothing met our standards for what good developer infrastructure should be.

So we built what we always wanted—a developer-first platform that makes agentic workflows composable, scalable, and effortless to ship.

**If no one else is going to build it right, we will.**

# **Get Started + Early YC Deal**

* **Quick install:** **_pip install dedalus-labs_**
* **Docs:** [docs.dedaluslabs.ai](http://docs.dedaluslabs.ai)
* **YC Deal:** we’re giving $200 free credits to every YC company. Email [founders@dedaluslabs.ai](mailto:founders@dedaluslabs.ai) to claim your deal!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94675&key=user_uploads/1126811/4a1b700a-a1ab-41a3-a730-7b9a88b65500)

_Let us build your wings_ so your agents can fly. 🪽

name: Cyberdesk
long_description:
Cyberdesk is the first self learning computer use agent for developers to automate desktop workflows. 

For example, one of our customers is building an AI agent for hospital patient intake, and they’re using us to automate an entire team of people manually clicking and typing into a desktop app to book appointments. 

We launched mid July, and our agent is already operating in production environments, creating appointments in electronic health record apps and processing files in legacy ERPs.

We’ve built the first computer use agent that memorizes tasks and repeats them quickly while still adapting to unexpected changes on the screen. A good analogy is to how humans use computers: once we get used to an app, we use it much faster, while still adapting to random popups and crashes. This new paradigm for computer use will be needed by every company automating human workflows on computers.

Mahmoud previously built robotic process automation solutions impacting 20K+ employees at a Fortune 100 company. He also built AI & ML solutions at Baylor College of Medicine Neuroscience & Texas Children's Hospital + co-published a paper at the Rice Networks Group. 

Alan is ex-NASA and previously dropped out to be the first founding engineer at a PearX startup. He is a second time founder, having previously built and scaled a consumer AI app to thousands of paying users.

Computer-use agents will automate the $6T dollars spent on enterprise knowledge work and Cyberdesk will be the platform to power this.

We’d love to talk with you!

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
We met 2 years ago, connecting over our shared experiences at Rice, and our love of building things. We both ended up living at the same Hacker House in Menlo Park, called Incepto! We started Cyberdesk with the realization that it’s really hard to build a great computer use agent, especially when it comes to reliability, speed, and cost. We both lived in a 9×9 Airbnb room with a tiny bed and a single desk (we call it the Cyberdesk lol) and got Cyberdesk off the ground, building the MVP in a 6 days and getting a paid customer the next day through a cold email. \
\
Cyberdesk was built to solve all three of the core problems with off the shelf computer use models: speed, reliability, and cost. We’re excited to deploy this architecture to the world and become the best developer framework for computer use.

It was a little over a month before the deadline for Summer 2025 came out when we started working together, so we got to work! We launched, got paid customers, and built out our infrastructure fast. A month later, we interviewed in person and got the call from Jon Xu the same night that we got in! It was one of the happiest days of our lives.

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer:
We started working together in late March (2025), with a shared goal of solving deep developer problems around computer use. We started off with an idea to help developers spin up virtual desktops for computer use agents in a single line of code. We shipped an MVP in 5 days and got a paid customer the next day through a cold email. For the next month, we kept shipping and looking for customers, and applied to YC with this idea. We found the product had interest from hobbyist developers, but for companies, there was much less pull because companies often already have VM infrastructure they are happy with. \
\
So we made the call to pivot. We talked to over 100 developers in the computer use and robotic process automation space, and heard the same thing over and over: automating Windows desktops is an important yet extremely tedious process. You create a script once, then it breaks every time something changes in the app or a popup happens. Computer use agents were meant to solve that pain but even they were slow, costly, and non deterministic. That’s how we came up with the idea for what Cyberdesk is today - a layer on top of computer use agents that helps it memorize tasks it’s done before and repeat it consistently, 3 - 5x faster, and cheaply, while still falling back to computer use during popups and anomalies. We built an MVP in a week, and got our first pilot a week later. \
\
Since then we’ve been rapidly building out the product and closing more deals with startups and companies in healthcare, construction, accounting, and more, all of them using our agent to automate manual computer work they’ve struggled to automate before.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
For a developer team to automate legacy desktop apps with poor APIs, they’ve often resorted to building brittle automation scripts (either in Python or using a legacy RPA tool like UiPath) or hiring unreliable remote workers to click on remote desktops. As they need to support more and more software and versions of that software, the development and maintenance times exponentially increases. \
\
Every company in the world has repetitive manual desktop work that is bogging them down. On top of that, companies building AI agents are increasingly having to interface with desktop apps to perform full human workflows. This problem is pervasive and we’re excited to solve it.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer: Traditional robotic process automation is a $6 billion industry, yet it only services a tiny fraction of desktop tasks that can now be automated by our agent. In the long term, our agent will automate every manual computer task.

Hey everyone! We’re Mahmoud and Alan, co-founders of Cyberdesk.

**🏆 TL;DR:**

We’re building a computer use agent for developers to automate legacy Windows apps like EHRs, ERPs, and more. Just write your task in plain English, and call our API to trigger our agent. Our agent is designed to follow memorized steps reliably, only falling back to computer use models during expected popups.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yCDGsiCNb3E

**❌ The Problem**

Developers in industries like healthcare, supply chain, and beyond often work with clients who have old, legacy Windows software. Today, to work with these clients, they probably:

* Hire unreliable offshore teams to manually click through remote desktops
* Write fragile automation scripts that break on popups and need constant fixes
* Skip the integration entirely—leaving valuable customers behind

**✨ Our Solution**

Just write your task in plain English, and our computer use agent will run it reliably, cheap, and fast, on any Windows PC (cloud or on prem).

Example: entering patient data into OpenDental, a legacy dental EHR (real use case from one of our customers)

1. **Write the task** (”Log in to Opendental, click Patients, find this dropdown, etc”), then just call our API to trigger the workflow
2. **Our agent learns the task.** Every time it repeats the task, it does it 100% deterministically, upwards of 3x faster, and almost zero cost
3. **If something unexpected happens** (like a popup), our system falls back to the computer use agent, and memorizes that trajectory too

launches.body:
Hey YC.

My name is Eshan. I’ve spent the last 5 years trying to address what I think is the most pressing problem in the country — addiction and mental health. Before YC, I ran a group doing on the ground overdose prevention work across the country. I also worked at the White House on Drug Policy.

**Insurance companies love to scrutinize behavioral health treatment**, partially because it’s expensive (a single 30-day residential treatment episode can cost upwards of $50,000), and partially because proving medical necessity for behavioral health is a subjective process.

But behavioral health care _is_ medically necessary. **Drug overdose is the single biggest cause of death for young people in the US.** And there are too many stories of insurers denying people care, only for those individuals to later lose their lives to overdose.

We were in the summer ‘25 YC batch. Since then, we’ve been working with a small group of customers to develop a new product. I’m excited to announce it today.\
\
**Introducing: Perspectives Reclaim**

Because they’re under so much pressure from payors, behavioral health treatment programs currently spend an immense amount of resources and staff generating documentation and auditing it to be perfect. \
\
Reclaim solves this by

1. Reading tens of thousands of pages of charts every night
2. Finding issues that can lead to insurance denials or other issues
3. Tracking down which clinician made the error and emailing back and forth with them until it’s solved.  

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=101622&key=user_uploads/2329278/a7ccf9c3-cf38-409a-a8d4-9c4421623a19)

\
In each of our pilots, we’ve flagged and resolved hundreds of issues, from missing documents to drug tests that weren’t happening when they were supposed to, **leading to more approvals from payors, higher revenue for our clinics, and better outcomes for patients.**

Reclaim’s agent can also help provide evidence when fighting against payor clawbacks and can generate the insurance documentation used to argue for more days of care.

In the last 4 weeks since launching Reclaim, we’ve gone from **0 —> $250k cARR.** Our vision is to replace the $30B spent on the financial and administrative services that keep these clinics afloat and give that capacity back to care.

**Asks**:

1. Intros to our ICP: we’re looking for multi-site behavioral health/SUD treatment centers that deal with commercial insurance.
2. We’re currently hiring a senior software engineer to help us scale. Any intros here would be appreciated.
3. Investor intros are always appreciated as well.

Here’s our launch video: <https://youtu.be/vvFe7AF3mUo>

launches.body:
**Perspectives Health is the AI assistant automating the admin work that slows down behavioral health clinics.**

[https://youtu.be/xL-XqY41L10](https://youtu.be/xL-XqY41L10%5C)

Hey everyone! We're Eshan and Kyle, founders of Perspectives Health.

We help the millions of clinicians and clinical directors finally use AI inside the outdated EMR systems they've been stuck in.

Most clinical record software works like Microsoft 95, has no modern APIs, and can't integrate with new tools. That leaves clinicians stuck doing endless manual computer work. 

Believe it or not, most behavioral health clinicians will spend 5 years of their lives just typing notes!

**The Problem**

* 60%+ of clinicians work outside of major hospital systems.
* Most of them use software that nobody can connect to.
* This means they can't access life-changing AI software, which could automate notes, billing, scheduling, and more.

**Our Solution**

* Connects to any web-based EMR instantly. Yes, we mean any EMR.
* Perspectives listens to sessions, writes notes better than a clinician, and populates them straight into any EMR. 
* No copy/paste. And we don't rely on browser agents, so our tool fills out any form in seconds, not minutes.

AI is rapidly improving, but most of healthcare is locked out due to legacy systems. Perspectives bridges that gap, making AI usable immediately. Clinicians want to help people. Not to be drowned in manual work. We're building toward a future where clinicians never touch a keyboard for documentation again—where intelligent systems handle every workflow outside of patient care. 

The first step is integrating seamlessly with outdated EMRs and filling in the critical workflows they lack. From there, we'll expand across specialties—behavioral health, speech therapy, physical therapy, veterinary care, and beyond—unlocking AI for every provider outside the hospital system.

**Our Traction**

* We're growing 25% every week.
* Once users try our product 5 times, the habit is built, and they never write notes without it.
* We have onboarded 9 clinics for our pilot program since YC started, and each is on track to onboard all our pilot clinicians by September (180 clinicians).

**Our Team**

Our founding team combines lived experience in mental health care, policy expertise from the White House Drug Policy team, and technical expertise in scalable AI systems.

**Our Ask**

If you're a behavioral health operator, clinician, or investor who believes AI should be helping providers now—not five years from now—let's talk.

Hey everyone, Ritanshu and Abhimanyu here from Questom.

We’re building **AI agents that handle the everyday conversations B2B companies rely on to sell.**\
\
[**Questom: AI Agents for Sales**](https://youtu.be/EkodDghaQ4A)

## **TL;DR**

Most B2B revenue still runs through **phone calls and emails**, not websites.

Teams struggle to:

* answer every inquiry
* follow up consistently
* collect details cleanly
* apply the right catalog + pricing rules
* generate accurate quotes
* and keep customers updated

Questom trains **AI sales agents** that do all of this automatically, using your workflows, your rules, your language, and your systems.

Our agents live directly inside the communication channels B2B teams already use:

**📞 Phone • 📧 Email • 💬 Chat • 📱 SMS**

They handle inbound conversations end-to-end and hand off to humans only when needed.

# **🚨 The Problem**

Across wholesalers, distributors, field-service companies, custom-order shops, foodservice, industrial supply, packaging, labels, and more — the story is the same:

**Revenue depends on conversations.**

Every day teams handle:

• “Can you do this?”

• “How much will it cost?”

• “Can I get it by Friday?”

• “Where’s my order?”

• “Can I change something?”

But these companies run lean.

Sales, operations, and customer service are often the _same people_ juggling:

* quoting
* re-quotes
* customer updates
* scheduling
* inventory/lead-time questions
* supplier coordination
* repeat jobs
* production constraints

When things get busy, response times slip, inboxes pile up, and high-intent buyers quietly move on.

This creates:

* Missed revenue
* Burnt-out teams
* Customers who don’t come back
* An invisible tax on growth

People think “chatbots” solve this, but bots don’t understand:

* catalogs
* pricing rules
* discounts
* exceptions
* minimums
* production timelines

B2B sales is _not_ FAQ automation.

It’s conversational problem-solving.

# **💡 The Solution**

**Questom builds AI sales agents that run your inbound sales process.**

They learn:

* your catalog
* your pricing
* your discounts & exceptions
* your constraints
* your approval flows
* your lead times
* your edge cases
* your CRM/ERP logic

The agent:

* answers instantly
* asks the right questions
* collects order requirements
* applies your pricing logic
* generates quotes and revisions
* manages follow-ups
* sends status updates
* and pushes structured orders into your ERP/CRM

When needed, the agent hand-offs to a human with full context, so nothing gets lost.

### **Operational impact:**

* Faster first responses
* Fewer missed inquiries
* More accurate quoting
* More deals closed
* Less repetitive messaging
* Happier customers
* Less load on your team

# **⚡ Early Results**

Across our pilots with wholesalers, print companies, and multi-location brands:

* Up to **50%** of inbound sales conversations fully automated
* Meaningful **AOV lift** from smart upsells
* Backlogs cleared within days
* More quotes sent → more revenue captured
* Teams finally able to focus on higher-value work

**Ritanshu** grew up in a 75-year-old wholesale business, worked at Google (Wing) and Tesla, and previously bootstrapped a SaaS product to $45K ARR.

**Abhimanyu** spent 7 years in Applied ML Research at Apple working on conversational intelligence, with CS degrees from IIT Kanpur and Columbia.

We’re combining **deep B2B operational understanding** with **real applied ML** to solve one of the oldest, hardest problems in the industry:

**turning everyday conversations into revenue automatically.**

launches.body:
Hey Everyone!

Excited to share our story and what we’ve been working on.

https://youtu.be/kdNXKa-zfcg

When Chan worked on Tesla’s Global Trade team, every car part—bolts, batteries, doors, etc—came from a different country. Each time tariffs shifted (pretty frequently), he and his team had to manually check thousands of parts across hundreds of pages of trade rules. Pair that with meetings with consultants, brokers, & suppliers to get potentially the worst workflow of 2025. All happening within Outlook & Excel 2019.\
They tried software, consultants, startups — every one of them got shot down due to reasons like product quality & data security, but mainly that it doesn’t bring enough value.

That’s why we built **MarkIt** — AI agents that actually _do the work_ for Suppliers, Brokers, and OEMs.

# **Introducing MarkIt - The Silver Bullet for Trade Compliance**

With agents that live where trade professionals already work — **Excel, broker portals, and browser** — MarkIt helps teams classify products, manage tariffs, and resolve customs issues in seconds, not hours.

# **MarkIt’s Value: Product & Logic Application**

MarkIt is intentionally lightweight, and customizable. Previously, without AI, software in this industry was clunky & typically automating a set workflow. Now, MarkIt services all of your workflow needs in a single

* **Classification**: MarkIt can enhance your workflows at scale. Entries are

  **defensible** with thorough **reasoning** and **supporting documents**.
* **OCR**: Upload your Bill of Ladings, Commercial Invoices, Packing Lists, and other documents to create your import filings and reports.
* **Customization**: Users can choose to **use their own logic**, where MarkIt’s platform would simply handle applying it at volume. No more worrying about reasonable care, if you don’t trust AI research.
* **Build Your Own:** MarkIt’s agents can work in files & desktop, applying trade logic in your own customizable way.
* **Integration:** Plug directly into ABIs and ERPs **only if you want.**

MarkIt is like a coworker specialized in customs & the trade process. Who’s willing to do all of your mindless “dishwashing” work.

# **Our Ask:**

We’re looking to connect with anyone who works in Global Trade. Suppliers, customs brokers, manufacturers, e-commerce operators, etc.

launches.tagline: An AI-native controls (SCADA) platform and integration service.
launches.body:
<https://youtu.be/DfSQ8L7d0BM?si=9Zp7BVPvCD_vB4ke>\
\
**THE PROBLEM**

Industrial control software still looks and feels like it was built in the Windows 95 era. Manufacturers spend weeks stitching together Programable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA), HMIs, databases, and custom integrations just to get systems running. Additionally, legacy systems collect enormous amounts of high-quality data, but don’t do _anything_ with it, even though it could easily be used for things such as anomaly detection or optimization recommendations.\
\
**OUR SOLUTION**

We're building an AI-native platform to unify the industrial control stack, starting with SCADA and eventually extending down to PLC hardware and the devices on the factory floor. We offer both a product and a service:

**1) Software**

We already built a full SCADA system to replace legacy platforms like Ignition, WinCC, and FactoryTalk. It’s AI native: users can use AI to generate controls screens in seconds (this used to take hours), write custom scrips/logical flows, and automatically detect issues before they become catastrophic. \
\
Not only is this a full SCADA system, but it can operate on top of an existing one so that users can take advantage of our “intelligence layer” without having to rip out their current infrastructure (people understandably don’t like doing this).\
\
**2) System Integration** 

We’ve recently expanded to become an AI-native industrial integrator. Instead of just selling our software, we integrate it into our clients existing stack for them, and help them set up any other tools they need to run it. 

Over the past few months, we've spent hundreds of hours talking with controls engineers, manufacturers, operators, and system integrators. We already knew that industrial software was broken, but we also learned that even when better technology exists, people are understandably cautious about adopting it. These systems run critical infrastructure and reliability matters more than novelty. Change is slow, but we want to reindustrialize America now.

**Instead of waiting for the industry to adopt an entirely new software stack, we're bringing our technology directly into customer projects today.**

While larger firms can spend millions on integration services, smaller firms don’t have that kind of money. Traditional integrators use highly manual methods to set up their clients software stacks (which are also outdated). By leveraging AI, we’ll be able to set up the same systems at 10x the speed and charge way less. 

**Our ask: if you’re exploring controls/automation systems, PLC programming, SCADA systems, or system integration**, **we’d love to talk. Or, if you know any deep tech companies that want to set up a controls system, let us know!**

See more at <https://controlseat.com>.

launches.tagline: The internal voice of the customer
launches.body:
# \*\*\*\*

**TL;DR: Your customer data is fragmented across Pylon, Granola, Posthog, Hubspot, Slack, and Notion. Poth connects that information into a living model of your customers, mapping analytics from Posthog and transcripts from Granola to the same customer, so you can finally answer the questions that live across multiple tools: churn, adoption or what to build next, with cited evidence. pothlabs.com**

<https://youtu.be/k9gsdaxXdtM>

**The problem:**

Companies have customer information scattered across support tickets, sales calls, CRM notes, surveys, interviews, product analytics and more. 

But answering a new question about customers still usually means manually searching across those systems or beginning another research project.

**The (soft) pivot:**

We originally built Poth to generate hypotheses and launch adaptive interviews and surveys to test them. To determine what questions to ask and which customers to ask, Poth first had to understand all of the customer information a company already had.

Under the hood, we built a customer knowledge graph: Poth identifies the important objects in a company’s data: customers, accounts, users, products, features, conversations, behaviors, and feedback, and connects them through their relationships.

As we integrated with more teams, we noticed that several were using this underlying model as much as, or more than, the survey functionality itself. They wanted to ask questions across everything their customers had already said and done so we made that a core part of the product!

**Customer knowledge graph example:**

For a company like Slack, Poth might model five objects:

* **Account**  (a company paying for Slack)
* **User**
* **Workspace**
* **Feature** (Slack Connect, Huddles, Canvas, or workflows)
* **Customer signal** (A support ticket, call transcript, survey response, or product event)

It then connects them through relationships such as:

User —BELONGS_TO→ Account Account —OWNS→ Workspace User —USED→ Feature Customer Signal —CREATED_BY→ User Customer Signal —REFERENCES→ Feature

Slack could then ask:

“Why are enterprise accounts trying Slack Connect but not adopting it broadly?”

And Poth could connect low Slack Connect usage in PostHog, permission-related support tickets in Pylon, security concerns mentioned in Granola transcripts, and renewal context from HubSpot, all through the same accounts, users, workspaces, and features.

Instead of returning a generic summary, Poth can show the supporting and contradicting evidence, cite the underlying sources, and explain what information is still missing.

In practice, the model contains many more objects and relationships based on each company’s business and data.

**Ask Poth:**

Connect your customer data sources and internal documentation. Poth automatically builds the living model, and your team can ask questions naturally across everything customers have said and done.

When the existing evidence is not enough, you can also use Poth to launch adaptive interviews and surveys to collect what is missing.

Some use cases we’ve seen:

* **Discovery:** “Across our discovery calls, what do users want most that we haven’t built?”
* **Adoption and growth:** What is preventing activated customers from adopting more of the product and expanding?”
* **Churn and risk:** “Identify the top three reasons customers have churned, then flag the five active accounts showing similar warning signs.”
* **Win-loss analysis:** “What are the most common reasons we lose enterprise deals, and which product gaps are actually affecting revenue?”
* **Account intelligence:** “Give me everything relevant to this account before my next customer call.”

**Our ask:**

We’re already working with several teams in the YC batch, and we’re looking for more companies whose customer context is spread across several systems.

I’d especially appreciate introductions to:

* Founders and product leaders at growing startups with significant customer data across three or more tools
* Heads of Customer Insights, Voice of the Customer, Customer Experience, User Research, or Customer Success at larger companies

And if your team has important customer questions it still cannot answer confidently, email me at [matthew@pothlabs.com](mailto:matthew@pothlabs.com)! We’ll work closely with early teams to connect their core systems and get them live.

pothlabs.com

**TL;DR: Marker partners with execs, learns how their organization actually works, finds the highest-impact problems, and solves them by** **shipping custom AI agents into production on the Marker platform in weeks. Each agent deepens our understanding of the business, so the next agent launches faster. We stay embedded until the business is rebuilt.**

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O829Y4wlKvk>

We’re Will Drevno, Richard Berwick, and David Pastewka, the founders of Marker. We’ve built together for 15 years. Our last company, Drapr (YC S20), was acquired by Gap Inc., and Richard went on to found Gap’s Office of AI.

## **Why we built Marker**

Inside Gap, we saw firsthand how much leaders wanted to transform their businesses with AI and how hard it was to turn that ambition into production systems that actually changed how their organizations worked.

**95% of AI initiatives still fail. Ours don’t.**

The hard part is understanding how work happens across people, systems, and teams; choosing the opportunities that matter most; and getting solutions into production.

## **How Marker works**

We embed with each company and lead the transformation end to end:

* **Understand the organization.** We listen closely to leaders and frontline teams, learn their systems and ways of working, and map the processes that usually live in people’s heads.
* **Find the biggest opportunities.** We identify and prioritize the problems where AI can have the greatest impact on cost, capacity, speed, or growth.
* **Build and ship.** We create custom agents and automations around the company’s real workflows and systems. The agents we deploy run on the Marker Command Center and go live in production within weeks.
* **Compound.** Every agent we deploy deepens our understanding of the company. That helps us launch the next one faster and makes Marker increasingly integral to how the organization operates.

## **Who we’re working with today**

We’re rebuilding companies from mid-size through Fortune 500.

## **Why us**

We’ve sat on every side of this: founders selling into enterprises, operators transforming one from the inside, and executives responsible for enterprise AI. Marker is the company we wish we could have hired at Gap.

**If you are (or you know) a leader looking for real AI transformation—not another pilot, deck, or self-serve tool—please send them our way.**

launches.tagline: Computer-use agents that work cross-border transaction alert investigations end to end: collect evidence, produce an assessment, draft an RFI.
launches.body:
We're building Zomma: AI operations employees for finance back offices, starting with cross-border transaction alert investigations.

**TL;DR:** Zomma agents work directly inside the software your ops team already uses. No APIs, no integrations. For every cross-border alert, the agent gathers the evidence, writes the draft assessment, and drafts the RFI, end-to-end. Running live compliance-ops pilots with a US RIA and a $10B AUM wealth tech. 92% on OSWorld.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDXDKH_tYhg>

## **The problem**

Cross-border payments trip more monitoring rules than anything else in the queue: sanctions name hits on foreign counterparties, high-risk corridors, first-time beneficiaries. Most alerts are false positives (McKinsey: over 90% in transaction monitoring), but every one still needs to be investigated. 20 to 60 minutes per case, across five or six systems, several with no API at all. And the evidence that clears them sits in foreign company registries and local-language adverse media. 

So review capacity scales the only way it can: hiring. When hiring lags volume, alerts pile into backlogs that take months to clear, and backlogs are what regulators fine: $3.8B in AML penalties last year alone.

## **What Zomma does**

Zomma agents work the queue on the same screens your analysts use: case manager, screening tool, admin panel, inbox, web search. Onboarding looks like hiring: an SOP and a login.

On a transaction monitoring alert, the agent

* pulls the KYC profile and payment history
* verifies the invoice and researches the counterparty, including registries you can only search by hand
* writes a case-specific assessment with every claim cited to the source screen
* drafts the RFI when documents are missing

Every step is logged and replayable: timestamped screenshots of every page checked, numbered citations, explicit no-match statements, a screen-by-screen trail an examiner can follow.

## **Why start with cross-border alerts**

If an employee can do it on a screen, Zomma can learn it: the rest of the compliance queue, payment disputes, client onboarding, trade ops. Cross-border alerts come first because they have the exact shape our agents are best at: high-volume, parallelizable work that needs real reasoning but follows a defined workflow to a documented disposition. They're also the hardest cases to automate any other way: the evidence lives in registries and portals that will never have APIs. And agents scale with the queue: a volume spike means provisioning two more that afternoon; a BPO batch takes a month to train.

Computer-use agents only recently got accurate enough to trust with a live queue, which is why we're building this now. Our state-of-the-art computer-use harness with our procedural and workflow memory system scores 92% on OSWorld.

## **Team**

* **Jihyun (CEO):** founding team at a Blackstone-backed hedge fund, scaled Asia's largest wealth tech, Goldman engineer.
* **Cash (CTO):** backend systems behind $20B+ in yearly transactions, trains VLMs for computer use.
* **Varun (CPO):** high-performance infra at Apple, design-verification agents at Bronco AI (YC S23).

Send us \~100 closed cross-border alerts and we'll show you what the agent would have done with them, or book a call: zommalabs.com/call.

launches.body:
Hey everyone! We’re David and Michael, co-founders of FlowManual.

**What FlowManual is**: AI preconstruction for General and MEP contractors, executing projects while cutting risk. 

**TL;DR:** Construction contractors waste hundreds of hours monthly on manual tasks, sifting through 500-page PDFs only to miss fine print that can cost tens of thousands. FlowManual automates the back-office work before and during construction, so teams can reliably secure and complete projects faster than ever before.

<https://youtu.be/aO5fBj_3kpU>\
\
**The Problem:**

Meet Jeremy. He’s a project manager at a mid-sized contractor, and his job is to secure projects and then make sure the company doesn’t lose money on already thin margins.

A bid invite lands in his inbox. To put together one number his firm can send in, Jeremy has to read thousands of pages. A 400-page project manual, drawings, insurance, spec sections, and so much more. Buried somewhere inside all this print is a line that can ultimately decide whether this job makes or loses money. From a liquidated-damages clause to a scope item sneakily handed to the mechanical contractor, if Jeremy misses it, it’s a $5K-$10K mistake.

Jeremy’s got one week, three other bids on his desk, and no way to read all of it as carefully as he’d like. So he reads what he can and sends in a number.

Say he wins. A change in the signed contract by the General Contractor or a sneaky difference in vendor pricing costs the company thousands after the fact. Every step of the way requires hundreds of pages of reading and referencing done under a deadline. And Jeremy does this for every job.

**The Solution:**\
FlowManual automates these historical workflows that contractors run on, allowing teams to submit bids and complete projects faster than ever before. Here’s a couple major features:

* AI Takeoffs from drawings
* Drawing comparisons / overlay
* Bid leveling
* Contract Review

Our software doesn’t do the job for you, but it works alongside you to reduce time spent and mistakes made.

**About Us:**\
Michael and David were college roommates and engineers at Harvard. When renovations for a heater in our dorm took 6 weeks, we poked at the problem, realizing it stems from a larger issue. Through hundreds of conversations with professionals, we found an industry that ran on file cabinets, Excel, and page-by-page manual review.\
\

* **Know anyone in construction?** Connections to anyone in the industry, including on the legal and tech side, is greatly appreciated. Anyone in Project Management, Business Development, Marketing, IT are ideal! Reach us at [founders@flowmanual.com](mailto:founders@flowmanual.com)

launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Title insurance is the thorn in the side of every single residential real estate transaction in America. With the home market bleeding, you'll find attorneys processing documents by hand with outdated software at title agencies. Vestris automates the back office and supplements processors the way software should — _letting shops give the same care to closing the biggest purchase of a buyer's life._

<https://youtu.be/u2do97AOvQY?si=JB78OAx5hDp80PXT>

### The Problem

Imagine you're shopping the market and you just found your dream home. You're ready to purchase, the contract is signed, everything is in place.

And you're recommended a settlement company, and told to buy title insurance.

Most homeowners couldn't tell you what title insurance actually buys them. In a nutshell: **you're paying for the peace of mind that the property you're buying has no open claims against it** — payments a title company makes on your behalf.

But it's also a process that takes weeks. Behind the phone, you've got lawyers processing files, manually checking emails, and scanning two seemingly identical documents for changes.

Meanwhile, the incumbent software is a decade-old, per-file database whose premium plans put it out of reach for the small and mid-size shops that make up most of the market.

### The Solution

Vestris runs the file end to end:

**Reads everything on arrival** — every document that hits a processor's inbox is routed to the right order, new contracts spin up new files, and the routine back-and-forth is handled, so the first 30% of a file is done before a human even looks.

**Does the math** — logs into county tax and land portals to pull up-to-date figures, then prorates taxes, utilities, HOA dues, and special assessments to the settlement date on that county's convention, every figure traced back to its source.

**Drafts the commitment** — building Schedule A from the vesting and legal description and Schedule B from the exceptions in the record, the work a small shop waits a week and pays an abstractor hundreds for.

**Closes it out** — reconciling the closing disclosure against the settlement statement, handling the lender back-and-forth, and showing the processor exactly what changed, so no one's squinting at two seemingly identical PDFs.

Every step still goes through human approval. What changes is bandwidth: **a mom-and-pop shop never has to turn down an order because they're swamped**, and they get to spend their time on the in-person care that made buyers seek them out in the first place.

### The Team

We're Aahil and Josh, best friends and UMich roommates.

Aahil previously built SafeKids and holds three USPTO patents. He spent the summer closing files at a title shop, seeing the processor's grind firsthand.

Josh previously built live-telemetry and communication systems for Michigan's Formula SAE team. He worked the same title desk, and stole the cubicle with the monitor 😠

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=109429&key=user_uploads/3411947/af48be0b-23b2-4cb5-9c1c-4eb5c7b45e50)

### Our Ask

We're running Vestris in parallel at a title shop that settles millions in deals a month.

If you know anyone at **a title agency, escrow, or settlement company** — we'd love an intro.

And if you've ever bought or sold a home, reach out! You probably have strong feelings about the title process :)

You can reach us at [founders@vestris.ai](mailto:founders@vestris.ai), or better yet, give us a call at +1 (571) 466 7878.

**TL;DR:** Chromie is the AI operating system for government contractors. We help teams find opportunities before the RFP drops, build the right relationships, test win strategies against real data, and draft winning proposals. All on top of a company brain that remembers everything your team has ever learned.

<https://youtu.be/6ZGxJlFgCgI>

\
**The problem**

The U.S. government is the largest buyer on earth, spending $800B on contracts every year. Yet the business is fundamentally relationship driven. Winning depends on understanding the agency, finding opportunities earlier than your competitors, and applying judgment built over years. 

Today, that work runs on gut instinct, fragmented tools, and institutional knowledge that disappears when people leave.

**What Chromie does**

Chromie surfaces agency signals and expiring contracts years before an RFP is posted publicly, giving capture teams time to understand the customer and shape a credible pursuit.

launches.tagline: Self-hosted agent harness for teams: sandboxed, policy-controlled, and never touching a real credential. Works from web and Slack.
launches.body:
Hi everyone 👋, we're Jonathan and Guy, founders of OneCLI.**\
\
🏆 TL;DR**

OneCLI is an open source agent harness for teams. Each employee gets their own sandboxed pro assistant agent, connected to their GitHub, Gmail, Notion, Dropbox, or CRM right from the chat/Slack, while the whole workspace runs under one policy your admins control. \
\
Agents never hold real secrets: the credential is injected at the network layer, per request, after the call is authorized. You can't steal what isn't there.

**Launch Video**\
<https://youtu.be/LUAMdqbl_Rw>

🚧 **The Problem**

Lately, autonomous agents have arrived and shown up everywhere. Tools like OpenClaw and Hermes have become extremely popular and been adopted by open source communities, mostly by individuals. Companies, however, have been left behind: they need integration with their identity providers to enable easy provisioning of agents on behalf of an employee's identity, with least-privilege access.

Those tools have fundamental flaws. Security fundamentals, like secret handling and organization-level control, are missing by default. So companies must choose between weak agents or making them powerful but risky.

✅ **What OneCLI Does**

OneCLI gives teams the whole harness, open source and self-hosted, so agents can be powerful and safe at once:

* **Sandboxed agent per employee:** each agent runs isolated with its own memory, skills, and permissions.
* **Secrets injected at the network layer:** the agent gets a placeholder, the gateway swaps in the real credential per request, after the call is authorized. Credentials never enter the agent's context, memory, or logs.
* **Policy enforced outside the model:** admins define org-wide policy. Block endpoints and scope access per agent.
* **Human-in-the-loop where it counts:** sensitive actions (send the email, delete the Linear ticket, empty the S3 bucket) wait for deterministic approval in the chat.
* **Full identity trail:** every agent is bound to an employee, every call logged with who it acted for and which policy allowed it.

🚀 **Team**

We've spent our careers in security. Jonathan built zero trust network access at Axis Security (acquired by HPE). The core ZTNA idea is that you never trust the client and enforce access outside it, at the network layer. Guy was the first employee at Argon (AppSec company acquired by Aqua Security), protecting client codebases. Agents need exactly the treatment ZTNA gives humans, so we built it.

🙏 **Our Ask**

* Do you want to provide each of your employees with a secure OpenClaw isolated in a sandbox? Shoot me an email: [jonathan@onecli.sh](mailto:jonathan@onecli.sh)
* Star/try the repo:[ https://github.com/onecli/onecli](https://github.com/onecli/onecli). Self-host in minutes, free.

launches.title: OneCLI - Your AI agents shouldn't be holding raw secrets
launches.tagline: Agents hold placeholder tokens, real secrets get injected at the network layer
launches.body:
# **🏆 TL;DR**

[**OneCLI**](http://onecli.sh) is an open-source credential gateway for **AI agents**.\
When an agent makes a call, OneCLI swaps in the real credential at the network layer and forwards it. The agent never touches the secret, **you can't steal what isn't there**.\
320K+ downloads, 2,500+ GitHub stars, and the default credential layer in NanoClaw (30K+ stars).

**Ask:** If your team runs coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) or autonomous agents in production. And if you can intro us to Head of DevOps or heads of DevSecOps at companies rolling out AI agents, email us at [jonathan@onecli.sh](mailto:jonathan@onecli.sh) \
\
**Sign up for free:** <https://onecli.sh>

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106907&key=user_uploads/406823/5294ff50-4b88-4ee7-9c9c-3c776b5b45b5)

<https://youtu.be/5e5pbPEzZfY>

# The Problem

AI agents are doing real work now, which means they need real credentials: API keys, database passwords, OAuth tokens. And there's no safe way to hand them over.

Today, every team does one of two things: hardcode secrets into **.env files** the agent can read, or build a one-off proxy hack. Both mean the **agent holds the secret**. An agent that holds a secret can leak it, through prompt injection, a malicious MCP server, a compromised dependency, or simply by pasting it into a log or a commit.

Secrets management was designed for humans and **deterministic software**. Autonomous agents that read untrusted webpages, install packages, and write their own code are a fundamentally different threat model. The blast radius of one leaked production key is enormous, and teams are granting agents more access every week.

# Our Solution

OneCLI moves the credential out of the agent entirely.

You run one command, and every outbound call from your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline) or autonomous agent (OpenClaw, Hermes, NanoClaw) routes through OneCLI. The agent only ever sees placeholder tokens. On each request, the proxy:

1. Matches the request by host/path
2. Checks it against policy
3. Swaps the placeholder for the real credential
4. Forwards the request

The agent never holds the secret, so there's nothing to steal, log, or exfiltrate. \
Secrets are AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest. The whole thing runs in a single Docker container with no external dependencies. It works with anything that can set HTTPS_PROXY.

For teams, we already support integration with IdPs and organization-wide policy setup, giving you full control and visibility over every access made by your agents.

# Why this and not the PAM/identity vendors?

Because the credential problem for agents is a **network problem, not an identity problem**. Vault-based tools (1Password, HashiCorp Vault) still hand the secret to the agent to authenticate. The agent holds it, so the agent can leak it. OneCLI injects the credential at the wire: transparent injection, policy enforced on every outbound request, and the secret never enters the agent's context in the first place.

# The Team

We've spent our careers in security. Guy (CTO) was the first hire at Argon (acquired by Aqua Security). Jonathan (CEO) worked on ZTNA and network security at Axis Security (acquired by HPE), after serving in Israeli Military Intelligence.

We hit this problem ourselves. Before OneCLI we built ChartDB together, an open-source database tool with 20K+ GitHub stars, and while building an agent orchestration layer on top of it, we kept hitting the same wall: there was no safe way to hand an autonomous agent credentials. Every team we talked to was either hardcoding API keys or duct-taping proxies. So we built the thing we wished existed.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=106907&key=user_uploads/406823/ff451063-51d2-4c13-9c5f-cd1863b8c648)

# The Ask

If you know a Head of DevOps or DevSecOps lead at a company rolling out AI agents, we'd love an intro.

[jonathan@onecli.sh](mailto:jonathan@onecli.sh)

👋 Hey friends, we're Nazz and Francisco. We spent years at HubSpot running its three largest customer platforms, and we're backed by HubSpot founder Dharmesh Shah.

**The problem: general-purpose agents aren't built for high-volume GTM**

The best GTM engineers can wire HubSpot, Clay, Outreach, Gong, and Slack into agents that run a revenue team. But run that same work through a general agent and it re-reasons every step, burns your entire weekly limit overnight, and still isn't reliable at volume. Almost nobody can hire enough GTM engineers to do it properly.

**How Nex works**

Describe a goal, and Nex builds and runs the workflow across 1000+ integrations:

* Lead generation, qualification, and enrichment
* Scraping public records
* Outbound over email and socials
* CRM cleanup and hygiene
* Re-engaging lost deals

Because most GTM work is repetitive and deterministic, Nex has AI write code for the predictable parts and run it fast without wasting tokens, saving AI judgment for the genuinely hard parts. That's how it breezes through high-volume work while not burning through your monthly AI budget in a day.

**What that looks like**

On a single onboarding call, Nex audited thousands of records in a customer's HubSpot, flagged missing data, archived owners, bad associations, and zombie deals, and started fixing them before the call was over.

**Why this matters**

GTM is the beachhead. The same engine runs any high-volume workflow that's too slow and too expensive to run straight through a general model, and that pattern shows up in every operations-heavy function: finance reconciliations, support triage, recruiting outreach.

launches.body:
Hey everyone. You’ve might of heard of Open AI, Open Router, OpenCode, OpenWork….

Introducing [OpenTag](https://www.tryopentag.com/?utm_source=yc&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=yc-launch&utm_content=launch-page) - the model agnostic Claude Tag.

We started early access a 2 weeks ago and are live with 10 teams.

If you've seen Claude Tag, you know the interface: tag an AI in Slack, hand it a task, get the result in the thread. We think that's the right interface. We built OpenTag because we think the multiplayer harness should be model agnostic. When a better model ships, your coworker gets better the same day, benefiting from the performance and cost improvements.

OpenTag is an AI coworker that lives inside of Slack. You invite it into the channels you want. It picks up how the company runs, how decisions are made, who owns what. It helps the team coordinate and builds automations for workflows that it sees as repetitive. It asks for tools and visibility the way an A-player hire does, and it tries to grow its own scope and agency. It starts as an intern and tries to earn the COO job. As it works, it writes a company wiki of how you actually run. That wiki compounds as a company brain, so OpenTag only gets sharper with time. Throw it anything. It does its best, and it asks for help when it’s blocked. The result lands in the thread, with sources, where the whole team can see it.

**Four parts, one coworker:**

1. **Ambient and proactive agents -** properly sandboxed with its own computer and browser, so you can trust them with actual tasks instead of babysitting chat windows.
2. **A wiki that maintains itself —** no more stale handbooks. OpenTag writes down how the company actually runs and keeps it current. Teammates can read it. Agents can read it.
3. **Automations that suggest themselves -** OpenTag watches how your team works and surfaces the repetitive stuff worth automating, so you're not designing workflows from a blank page.
4. **Built for multiplayer** - OpenTag is designed with proper permissioning that matches how your team operates.

**2 minutes to start.** Add OpenTag to Slack, invite it to the channels where work happens, give it a job. It’ll ask for the tools it needs (whatever the job touches). It only reads the channels you invited it to.

**Built by software engineers who’ve shipped products used by millions.**

The three of us worked together at Lilac Labs (YC S24) and all went to Berkeley. Tony (CEO) was software at Tesla and Intel. Shelden (CTO) was at Flatiron Health, Roche, and Certik (cyber security). Wilson (Chief Engineer) was at Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Vestible, a regulated securities platform.

OpenTag is the coworker we wanted at our last company, when we were the ones running every job.

**Try OpenTag today**

Try it at [www.tryopentag.com](http://www.tryopentag.com)

Take 30 minutes with me: [book a demo.](https://cal.com/tony-kam-ympx2p/intro?overlayCalendar=true)

Would love to hear your thoughts and feedback. You can email me at [tony@tryopentag.com](mailto:tony@tryopentag.com)
